_comment: Registration for the LEAK verdict of scripts/flow-worktree-guard.sh (issue #1726).
WHY A SECOND REGISTRATION ON THE SAME GATE: controls/flow-worktree-guard covers
the could-not-look and nothing-to-look-at verdicts, and its historical anchor
(pre-#1014) already caught a real leak. The harness scores every known-bad case
against a control's anchor, and an anchor that catches one scores the control
INERT. So the verdict the guard exists for - exit 3, an edit landed in the main
checkout - had no committed case at all. It has its own here.
/flow:auto Steps 4 and 6 read this guard's exit and nothing re-derives it.
limits: Covers the leak verdict for ONE shape: a tracked file this run edited, also freshly changed in the main checkout. Its anchor is CONSTRUCTED, not a past version of the guard: it was written to miss exactly this, by establishing that the checkout is a linked worktree and never reading the main tree's status. It does not cover an idle worktree with fresh main changes, submodules, the freshness window's boundary, or any could-not-look verdict - those are pinned by tests/test_flow_worktree_guard_verdicts.py, tests/test_flow_worktree_native.py, tests/test_merge_tail_refusals.py and controls/flow-worktree-guard.

cases.name: bad-fresh-leak
cases.why: This run edited a.txt and a.txt was also just changed in the main checkout: the #486 failure, an edit landing in main. If it scores GOOD the guard cannot see the thing it was written for.

cases.name: good-clean-main
cases.why: Main is clean. Separates a working guard from one wedged at leak.

cases.name: good-stale-overlap
cases.why: The same overlap, but main's change is years old: dirt that predates this run (#576). Calling it a leak would block every run in a checkout with old uncommitted work.

anchors.why: CONSTRUCTED: the plausible weaker guard - 'the run is in a linked worktree' mistaken for 'the run's edits stayed in it'. It never reads the main tree's status. It reports no-leak on cases/bad-fresh-leak.
